name: Rogue
summary: Across Azeroth, Rogues choose when to face danger and when to slip away unseen. Light leather, paired blades, and brewed toxins let them strike before foes can react. They serve as scouts, assassins, pickpockets, and agents of factions and hidden syndicates.

sections.title: Strike from the Shadows
sections.body: Rogues favor quiet, quick attacks over the open clashes of frontline warriors. In light leather, they stalk their quarry unseen. When an opening comes, they strike with precision at vital organs or exposed joints. A swift chain of blows weakens an enemy, and a finishing strike can end the fight.

sections.title: Poisons and Street Smarts
sections.body: A blade alone rarely serves a cutpurse or killer. Rogues brew venoms to numb limbs, slow an escape, or drain a target's strength. Lockpicks, thrown weapons, and tricks that draw attention elsewhere help them slip past guarded walls, disarm traps, and enter vaults that would confound a company of soldiers.

sections.title: Guilds, Crowns, and Syndicates
sections.body: Many rogues work alone as highwaymen or street thugs. The finest join intelligence networks and assassin guilds. Stormwind relies on SI:7, while the Forsaken rely on the relentless Deathstalkers. In Orgrimmar, remnants of the Shattered Hand serve the Warchief. The neutral League of Assassins answers to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt.

faq.q: What armor and weapons do rogues use?
faq.answer: Rogues wear leather armor and favor one-handed weapons, often wielding a blade in each hand. They use daggers, swords, maces, and fist weapons. For ranged attacks, they carry throwing knives, bows, or crossbows.

faq.q: How does stealth work for a rogue?
faq.answer: A rogue uses quiet steps and shadow to pass unseen from a distance. An alert guard or enemy may spot one who moves too close. From stealth, rogues can get behind a foe and strike with ambushes, garrotes, or blows that disable.

The League of Assassins is an ancient, secretive brotherhood based at Ravenholdt Manor in the Alterac Mountains and led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. Free of faction ties, the guild devotes itself to the discipline, honor, and business of assassination. It takes contracts without regard to political allegiance.

SI:7 is Stormwind's chief covert intelligence and reconnaissance wing, based in Stormwind City. Its field agents, snipers, and thieves carry out espionage, high-profile assassinations, and border reconnaissance to protect Alliance interests across Azeroth.

faq.q: How do rogues fight in prolonged combat?
faq.answer: When a first strike fails to end a fight, rogues use agility and footwork to avoid counterblows. They attack in quick succession with paired weapons, find openings, then finish with lethal moves such as ruptures or eviscerations.

Most rogues depend on physical conditioning, martial training, alchemy, and ordinary stealth. Skilled practitioners may also use minor mysticism or shadow magic to conceal themselves, slip into shadows in daylight, or vanish from sight.
All races except the tauren can be rogues: humans, dwarves, gnomes, and night elves in the Alliance; orcs, trolls, and the Forsaken in the Horde; and the Skyborne on either side.

angles.text: As a rogue, you rely on patience and precision, whether you serve high command or pick pockets in city alleys.
The Alliance's covert strength includes Stormwind's SI:7, which handles threats within its borders and beyond them.
The Horde relies on the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar and Sylvanas Windrunner's feared Deathstalkers in the Undercity to scout enemy territory and quietly eliminate threats.
